_doc: Stream E (owner feedback 7, V2 — E leads the economy). Every gold number a PLACE or a PERSON pays or charges; js/sim/economy-knobs.js reads it (same defaults as before when a key is missing) and tools/sim-economy.mjs measures the result: `node tools/sim-economy.mjs` prints gold per hour by activity and the price ladder. What a KILL pays and what an ITEM is worth are stream C's (data/rules/prices.json), a catch's gold is C's data/rules/fishing.json `value` over the species prices in data/provinces/angling.json, shop goods prices are data/provinces/shops.json. THE RULES these numbers serve are in `targets` and are what tests/E/playtest7-economy.test.js pins — ratios, never the numbers.

unit._doc: ONE KILL'S GOLD at a level — the same numbers as stream C's data/rules/prices.json `kill` (rules.killGold(level)); a test keeps the two equal, so there is no second table. Quest purses are reward.gold x unit x quest.mult.

quest._doc: a quest's purse = reward.gold (6-10 for an errand, 20-50 for a dungeon or story step) x one kill's gold x this. xpMult (owner feedback 8, W4): a hand-in pays reward.xp x the level span x stream C questMult x THIS. Stream C raised kill experience x1.5 at levels 1-6; without this an hour of questing levelled you SLOWER than an hour of standing in a camp at every level up to 6 (x0.64-0.9). `node tools/sim-economy.mjs --curve` prints the table.

event._doc: an event's gold = reward.gold x (1 + perLevel x (level - 1)) x mult (x the length factor, x2 for the world boss). It was perLevel 0.15, mult 1: a level-10 zone event paid 28 gold.

chest._doc: a dungeon's reward chest / a vignette chest. It was 5 + 4 x level.

fare._doc: Y31 (owner feedback 10): 6 + metres / 135 -> 3 + metres / 200 (2 km 21 -> 13 gold, 8 km 65 -> 43): a waystone hop was twelve minutes of real play at level 1. Still dearer than the ox-cart over the same road (cart: 3 + metres / 250).

sell._doc: what a merchant pays for gear as a share of its list price — stream C's prices.json gear.sellFactor is the one the rules use; keep the two the same. A fish sells for its own price.

targets._doc: The rules. Y31 (owner feedback 10) restated the price ladder in MINUTES OF REAL PLAY (tools/sim-economy.mjs ASSUME.real over the one income table, data/rules/prices.json income.lifetime): `uncommonMinutes` / `rareMinutes` = how long a character plays to afford one shop piece of its own level; `potionMinutesMax` = a healing potion costs no more than this many minutes at any level (level 1 is the poorest); `sellBack` = what a merchant pays as a share of the price; `soldShareMax` = sold loot is never more than this share of an hour's income; `mountHours` = real hours of play a mount costs at the level it opens; `ownerPoint` = the measured point the sim must reproduce (gold in total on reaching `level`, within `tolerance`). The older ratios compare one activity with another in the same IDEAL hour and stand as they were. cartShare: a ride to the NEXT town costs this share of an hour of questing at level 1 (the poorest rider). cartFarthestShare: the dearest ride in the province costs at most this share of a level-1 hour.

questXp._doc: W4: at every level in `levels`, an hour of questing gives at least questingOverKilling[0] of the experience of an hour of pure killing (and never more than [1] — kills must stay a fair share), and hand-ins are handInShare of a questing hour.

barber._mult: owner feedback 9 (X4, dev report #16): the barber is free for now. mult multiplies every price below; 1 = these prices, 0 = free.

cart._doc: W5 (owner feedback 8): an ox-cart ride. cartFare(metres of road) = max(minGold, round(base + metres / metresPerGold)); the table for every pair of towns is data/provinces/carts.json `fares` (tools/content-towns.mjs). Cheaper than a waystone over the same road (`fare`), and it takes you to a town you have never seen.
